newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq delists Holly Holdings stock.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq delists Holly Holdings stock.

text.p: The Nasdaq Stock Market said on Thursday that it delisted Holly Holdings Inc from its Smallcap Market.

A Nasdaq spokesman said Holly Holdings was delisted "for reasons concerning the public interest and voting rights." The spokesman refused to comment further, citing Nasdaq's policy not to discuss the specifics of its rulings.
Holly Holdings waved its opportunity for an appeal hearing scheduled for today, according to a company attorney.
"We had no shot at winning an appeal," the lawyer said.

In an earlier press release, Holly said it is requesting that its market-makers file Securities and Exchange Commission Form 211 with the National Association of Securities Dealers (NASD) immediately in order for the common stock to resume trading on the OTC Bulletin Board. Market makers submit the form on behalf of a stock they want quoted on the OTC Bulliten Board.
"This is the fastest way to get it back on the board," the lawyer said. The company hopes the stock will resume trading sometime next week.
According to the Holly Holdings lawyer, the Nasdaq was concerned because, "of the dilution of shares through some regulation S offerings, and the company's past history of losses."
Commenting on the delisting, Holly president William Patrowicz told Reuters, "There's no problem with us. We just got $65 million in financing to build the largest casino in the state of Colorado."
Country World Casino, which is controlled by Holly, signed a financing agreement to build the casino in Black Hawk, Colo., Thursday.
In March, Holly brought Country World out of Chapter 11 bankruptcy. The company said it has paid Country World's creditors in full.
